title: The communion of saints, again
hook: the saints you've met these five years are your company
tomorrow: why does every Hail Mary end at a deathbed?

segments.voice: Yesterday's line: what no eye has seen. Heaven is bigger than any picture of it. And it isn't empty. It's full of people.
screen: `WHAT NO EYE HAS SEEN.` → `FULL OF PEOPLE.`

segments.voice: Scroll your contacts and you'll find a strange history: a coach from middle school, a cousin's ex, someone saved only as Dentist. The people who actually keep you company are fewer, and you'd know them by voice. This path has been adding names you didn't have: Teresa of Ávila, who described prayer as friendship. Joseph, who said nothing and stayed. A whole crowd. The letter to the Hebrews has a word for them.
screen: `YOUR CONTACTS, A STRANGE HISTORY.` → `NAMES THIS PATH ADDED.` → `A WHOLE CROWD.`

segments.voice: It says, in the Douay-Rheims, that we have "so great a cloud of witnesses over our head." Some readers hear a stadium: a crowd around the race, calling your name. The Church gives that crowd a sound. At the Easter Vigil, at baptisms, at ordinations, a cantor sings the Litany of the Saints. A name, and the whole church answers: pray for us. Holy Mary, pray for us. Saint Joseph, pray for us. Name after name, until the room fills up. That's the communion of saints, in your own voice. It has a smell too: the candle lit in front of a statue, still burning after you've gone home. And it has objects: the holy card in a wallet, the medal on a chain. Now the popular mix-up: people think Catholics worship saints. The Church says no. Worship is for God alone. Asking a saint to pray for you is like asking a friend, except this friend is alive in God and has finished the race. And notice how the Litany ends: with the people turning to God himself, asking him to hear them. The saints aren't statues, and they aren't the destination. They're company on the way.
screen: `A CLOUD OF WITNESSES.` · `THE LITANY: PRAY FOR US.` · `A CANDLE, A CARD, A MEDAL.` · `WORSHIP IS FOR GOD ALONE.` · then, large: `MY COMPANY.`

segments.voice: Take a pen and write three saints' names down the side of a page, ones you've met on this path or grew up with. Say each one out loud, and answer it yourself, the way the Litany does: pray for us. Take your time with each name.
The communion of saints. The living, the dead and the saints in heaven, one family, praying for one another.
Pocket this one: my company, a crowd that already knows your name and keeps it. Talk tomorrow.

screen: `DAY 1726 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: WHY DOES EVERY HAIL MARY END AT A DEATHBED?`

howItsDone: Catholics ask the saints to pray for them, light candles before their images, keep holy cards and medals, and sing the Litany of the Saints at the Easter Vigil, baptisms and ordinations.
